text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Prime Minister Netanyahu seeks to improve ties with Amman.
- Erez talks fail to show substantial progress.
- Palestinian President Arafat to Israeli President Weizman: Shooting will stop.
- Coordinator in West Bank and Gaza, Major-General Oren Shahor, says flare-up could end peacemaking.
- Finance Minister Dan Meridor considers increased budget cuts in 1997.
- Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon mulls new railways in areas, into Jordan.
- Embassies instructed to spruce up Israel's image following unrest.
- Record provident fund withdrawals last month.
- Israel Corporation seeks foreign partner for Zim.
- Internet company, Delta Three of Jerusalem, to offer phone-to-phone service.
- Only 25 percent of firms with state aid meet job, export targets.
- Two bids made for United Mizrahi Bank's American subsidiary.
GLOBES
- Netanyahu assembles the economic hierarchy and Meridor says there could be an even bigger cut in the 1997 budget.
- Sharon: There's no problem of investors' withdrawal because of the situation in the territories.
HAARETZ
- Netanyahu convenes inner cabinet for a special discussion on the crisis in relations with Jordan.

- Aides to prime minister: Netanyahu told Rabbi Ovadia Yosef he is ready to consider positively bringing Labour into his government. Labour official: "We've been in this movie dozens of times before."
- Southern army commander says another agreement is urgent that would answer security problems.
- Netanyahu and Defence Minister Mordechai decide to leave reinforcements on the Golan. Assessment in Israel: Syrian President Assad could take military action after U.S. elections.
- Meridor worried about a freeze in exports, says economy in slowdown.
- Mother of Moroccan waiter killed by Mossad 23 years ago in Lillehammer wants compensation the same as his widow and children received.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Conciliation effort with King Hussein.
- On Sunday a mosque will open on Temple Mount, Shin Bet has warned of right-wing Israeli response.
- Meridor: Pace of growth in 1996 -- four percent.
- Pressures on Sara Netanyahu's former husband not to publish a book he plans on her.
MAARIV
- Effort to prevent crisis in Israel-Jordan ties.
